summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute pancreatitis with dehydration and no IV access, following a typical flare of epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had recently completed treatment for Herbaspirillum bacteremia from a previous port-a-cath infection. Blood cultures on admission were negative, and diarrhea resolved with a negative C. difficile test. A double-lumen tunneled central line was placed via the right subclavian vein to enable home IV hydration and reduce readmissions. Warfarin was restarted due to extensive upper extremity venous thrombosis history, and amlodipine replaced lisinopril for hypertension to avoid potential pancreatitis triggers. Iron infusion was given for iron deficiency anemia. The patient improved with pain and nausea control, advanced to a regular diet, and was discharged home with home health services, ethanol locks for line maintenance, and a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
